task: Connect the council referee to the orchestrator so Claude Code, Copilot CLI and plain terminals all plan requests the same way

independent.stance: One dispatch module, three thin entry points.
keyArguments: The old router sends nearly every request to the implementation agent (VERIFIED_FACT: route_request output for three sample tasks).
The referee already classifies tiers and convenes personas, so a dispatch module only needs to combine it with lifecycle state.
assumptions: The referee's tier is good enough to be authoritative (ASSUMPTION).

independent.stance: Do not build a second router; reuse the one that works.
keyArguments: Keeping both routers fully active doubles the rules to maintain.
Each client should call the same Python code rather than re-implement routing in JavaScript.
risks: Copy-pasted routing logic in the website or installer would drift.
assumptions: Python 3.10 is available wherever the CLI runs (ASSUMPTION).

independent.stance: Expose planning as a read-only MCP tool.
keyArguments: Copilot CLI and other clients add stdio MCP servers with `copilot mcp add`, so an MCP tool reaches them without a custom adapter (VERIFIED_FACT: GitHub Copilot CLI docs).
A read-only tool needs no new permission model.
risks: Tool-count assertions in the MCP tests will need updating.
assumptions: Clients pass plain-text tasks under 2000 characters (ASSUMPTION).
evidence: docs.github.com: Adding MCP servers for GitHub Copilot CLI

keyArguments: `cli.js ask "..."` is easier to remember than a Python module path.
The installed /orchestrator command should contain the real path to the framework so it works from any project.
risks: Users without python3 on PATH get a confusing error.
assumptions: Most users install from a clone (VERIFIED_FACT: package is not on npm).

independent.stance: Planning must stay read-only and bounded.
keyArguments: The plan reads framework files only and writes nothing.
Task text goes to Python as an argument list, never through a shell.
risks: A website endpoint that runs Python could be abused if exposed beyond localhost.
assumptions: The site server is local only (ASSUMPTION).

challenges.critique: Keeping the old router as a peer creates two answers to the same question.
challenges.counterProposal: Make the referee's tier authoritative and use the old router only as a fallback when no council matches.

challenges.critique: A separate JavaScript implementation of `ask` would duplicate the Python logic.
challenges.counterProposal: Have `cli.js ask` spawn the Python dispatcher and print its output.

challenges.critique: A website endpoint that runs the planner must not accept unbounded input.
challenges.counterProposal: Cap task length and pass it as an argument, with no shell, from the local server only.

challenges.critique: Piloting first delays the Copilot CLI path, which needs nothing beyond the MCP tool.
challenges.counterProposal: Ship the MCP tool and CLI together; they share the same dispatcher.

whatChanged: The referee's tier is authoritative; the old router is a fallback.
whatRemainedUnchanged: One dispatch module with three entry points.

responses.reason: One answer per request is simpler to trust.

whatChanged: Agrees to ship the MCP tool and CLI together because both call the same code.

responses.reason: No duplicated logic, so no reason to stage it.

whatChanged: Task length is capped at 2000 characters for the website and MCP.
whatRemainedUnchanged: Installed /orchestrator command uses the real path to the framework.

strongestArgumentsFor: Every client gets the same plan from one dispatcher.
Copilot CLI and other MCP clients need only the read-only plan_task tool.
strongestArgumentsAgainst: Requires python3 wherever the CLI runs.

evidence.statement: The old router assigned all three sample tasks to the implementation agent.
Copilot CLI adds stdio MCP servers with `copilot mcp add NAME -- COMMAND`.

assumptions: Python 3.10 or later is installed where the CLI runs.
unknowns: How often the referee's keyword routing picks a weaker specialist than a person would.

tradeOffs.sacrificed: The old router's persona choice for council-sized tasks
A pure JavaScript CLI with no Python requirement

risks.description: Keyword routing picks the wrong specialist

mitigations: Cap task length, pass arguments without a shell, and document the server as local only.
Users can name a council or persona explicitly with the referee CLI.
mvpScope: Installed /orchestrator command and skill call the dispatcher
excludedScope: Running persona rounds automatically without a model

validationExperiments.experiment: Plan the same task through cli.js ask, plan_task over MCP stdio and the website endpoint
validationExperiments.passMetric: Same tier and convened personas in all three

conditionsToChange: Routing mistakes become common enough to justify a model-based classifier.
